observations.text: SP, due to insufficient study of the formation visual signals of the syllabus, could not execute the signals addressed to Lead without assistance, with the result that the IP had to direct and execute part of the signal exchange from the rear cockpit. The signals were neither shaped nor held long enough to be perceivable from the other member of formation. Further study of the visual signals is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, did not apprehend the fuel check signal passed by Lead and did not confirm with a visual signal that it had been understood, with the result that the IP had to direct the response. The exchange was completed only after the IP's intervention.

SP executed and apprehended the visual signals as Wingman within the standards of the Training Section for this block, completing the exchanges after the IP's verbal prompts. Two signals addressed to the SP were acknowledged with delay, and the confirming visual signal was given only after a reminder. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness in apprehending and confirming the signals is expected to improve.

SP knew and executed the visual signals as Wingman, shaping them so that they were perceivable from the other member of formation beyond doubt. Minor delays in initiating two signals were recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without the IP's verbal prompts. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew and executed all the visual signals of the sortie accurately and promptly, both toward the other member of formation and toward the tower. Each signal addressed to the SP was apprehended and confirmed with the prescribed visual signal, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed all the visual signals with exceptional accuracy, presenting them within the field of view of the other member of formation and holding them so that they were perceivable beyond doubt. Every signal addressed to the SP was apprehended immediately and confirmed with the corresponding visual signal, with negligible delay. Performance was above the desired levels for the Training Section, both as Leader and as Wingman. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized technique in presenting the visual signals, gave them below the canopy rail and outside the field of view of the other member of formation, with the result that the signals were not perceivable beyond doubt. SP could not complete the exchange without assistance and the IP directed the signal sequence. Further practice of the visual signals as Leader and as Wingman is required.

SP, due to failure to pass a required call at the briefed point, did not execute the visual signal foreseen for the configuration change and did not confirm the signal addressed by Lead, with the result that the IP had to execute the exchange. The formation continued in the previous configuration until the IP intervened.

SP, due to a hand position that did not clear the instrument coaming, executed the visual signals in a way that was not perceivable from the other member of formation, with the result that two signals had to be repeated by Lead. The exchange was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the error was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the exchange, did not apprehend the visual signal addressed by Lead and did not confirm it with the prescribed visual signal, with the result that the response was given only after the IP's verbal prompt. Recognition of the signal was delayed by several seconds.

SP executed and apprehended the visual signals within the desired standards as Wingman, without the IP's intervention. However, two signals were initially shaped imprecisely and were re-presented on the SP's own initiative before Lead responded, and the confirming signal was given late on one occasion. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in the presentation of the signals is expected to improve.

SP knew and executed all the visual signals accurately and promptly, both as Leader and as Wingman, in a way that was perceivable from the other member of formation beyond doubt. Every signal addressed to the SP was confirmed with the corresponding visual signal, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional accuracy in the execution of the visual signals, presenting each one clearly within the field of view of the other member of formation and toward the tower where required. Apprehension of the signals addressed to the SP was immediate and each was confirmed with the prescribed visual signal, with negligible delay throughout the sortie. Performance exceeded the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to confusion between the visual signal for the fuel check and the signal for the lead change, executed a signal that did not correspond to the intended action, with the result that the formation did not complete the intended sequence and the IP had to execute the correct signal. SP could not resolve the exchange without assistance. Further study of the visual signals is required.

SP, due to an uncoordinated response between the two cockpits during the procedure, did not apprehend the visual signals addressed by Lead and did not confirm that they had been understood, with the result that the IP directed and executed part of the exchange. The formation position was corrected by Lead before the sequence could continue.

SP, due to signals that were not held long enough to be read by the other member of formation, did not execute the visual signals in a way perceivable beyond doubt, with the result that three signals required repetition by Lead. The exchange was completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of the error.

SP, due to complacency on an exchange flown repeatedly without difficulty, did not confirm with a visual signal that the signals addressed to the SP had been understood, with the result that Lead repeated each signal before proceeding. The omission was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to an initially imprecise shaping of the visual signals as Leader, gave two signals that were not immediately perceivable from the Wingman, with the result of a short delay in the formation response. Both signals were re-presented correctly on the SP's own initiative, in a timely manner and without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to situational awareness limited to the instrument in use, did not apprehend one visual signal addressed by Lead at the briefed point, with the result that the confirming visual signal was given late. The omission was recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention.

SP executed and apprehended all the visual signals accurately and promptly, as Leader and as Wingman, without the IP's intervention. However, the confirming signal was twice given only after Lead had repeated the signal, and one signal toward the tower was presented at the edge of the required field of view. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more consistent presentation and an immediate confirmation of the signals are expected to improve.

SP knew and executed all the visual signals with exceptional accuracy, presenting each one clearly and unambiguously to the other member of formation and to the tower. Every signal addressed to the SP was apprehended immediately and confirmed with the prescribed visual signal, with negligible delay in every exchange of the sortie. Performance was above the desired levels for the Training Section, both as Leader and as Wingman. Above end of block MIF achieved.
